correctness.rationale: The published vertex description reduces every vertex to one of n+1 permutation layers. Uniqueness of the Euclidean minimum enclosing ball and full coordinate-permutation symmetry force a diagonal center. For translated center s1, the layer squared distances are Q_k(s)=n s^2-2S_k s+T_k and satisfy Q_k-Q_{k+1}=lambda_k(lambda_k-2s), so the active layer changes monotonically with s. On each active interval Q_k is a convex quadratic with minimizer S_k/n. The endpoint tests are exactly D_k and nb-D_k, while D_k is strictly decreasing, yielding the stated K and s_* without omitted cases. Substitution gives R^2 and the contact layers; the classical quadratic threshold gives the golden-ratio limit.

value.rationale: Parking-function polytopes are an actively studied family with established face, volume, generalized-permutahedron, polymatroid, and walk-diameter theories. The theorem supplies their exact outer Euclidean size and unique outer center throughout the full two-parameter family. It also identifies precisely which vertex layer controls the circumsphere and reveals a non-obvious golden-ratio layer in the classical family. This is a family-wide structural metric classification, not a finite table or a routine reformulation of the existing inradius result.
